page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-4 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine featuring one NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture with 24 GB of VRAM. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor providing 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It operates at a clock speed of 2.2 GHz and includes 16.0 GB of system memory, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. No local NVMe storage is bundled with this configuration.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. The CPU performance is consistently positioned in the bottom 25% across stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark suites, with multi-core and single-core metrics indicating limited raw compute capacity. Similarly, memory bandwidth and file decompression speeds fall into the lower tiers. However, the integrated NVIDIA L4 GPU delivers top-tier performance in the top 10% for large language model inference. Prompt processing and text generation speeds for both small and medium models are highly optimized.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g2-standard-4 offers a specialized resource profile. While the host CPU and memory resources are modest and exhibit lower performance-per-resource ratios for general-purpose computing, the inclusion of a 24 GB VRAM GPU makes it a highly cost-effective entry point for machine learning inference and graphics workloads. It is poorly suited for CPU-heavy compilation, database operations, or high-throughput web serving. Instead, this server is optimized for small-to-medium LLM inference, AI-driven text generation, and GPU-accelerated graphics processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-4 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine designed for GPU-accelerated workloads. It features a single NVIDIA L4 GPU with 24 GB of VRAM, paired with 4 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs running at 2.2 GHz and 16.0 GB of system memory. The instance does not include local storage. While CPU-based benchmarks place the processor performance in the bottom 25%, the GPU delivers top-tier performance in the top 10% for LLM inference. Specifically, prompt processing and text generation for 135M and 7B models are highly efficient. Consequently, this server is best suited for machine learning inference, small-to-medium AI model deployment, and graphics rendering, rather than general-purpose or CPU-intensive computing.
